items.title: Implement the consent ledger, purpose registry, data-principal rights and retention jobs
items.outcome: As a person using PenniLogic, I can see what I consented to, withdraw any of it, request access, correction or erasure, and have my data actually deleted on a schedule, so that the product is lawfully operable before the first beta user is onboarded.
items.context: Consent, rights and retention are currently scheduled after the beta, which means real people would be onboarded before the obligations they trigger are implemented. The retention schedule also exists only as a document, and an unenforced schedule is not a schedule.
scope: Purpose registry describing each processing purpose in plain language with a version
Consent ledger recording grant and withdrawal with timestamp, purpose and version, append only
Access, correction and erasure request endpoints with a defined service level and status tracking
Retention jobs per data class that delete or anonymise on schedule and record what they did
Propagation of correction and erasure to derived tables, caches, search indexes, vector or embedding stores and assistant conversation records
Grievance channel and named grievance officer, published with the contact route and the response clock
Response clock per request type, started at acknowledgement, with escalation when it is missed
acceptance_criteria: No processing path can run without a recorded, unexpired consent for its purpose, proven by a negative test
Withdrawing consent stops the corresponding processing immediately and the ledger records it
An access request returns a complete, machine-readable dataset within the published service level
A correction propagates to derived data and the propagation is verifiable
Any assistant conversation storage is separately consented, appears in the purpose and retention registries, contains no raw message content, and is included in export and erasure
An erasure request completes within the published service level and is verified by the erasure harness
Retention jobs are idempotent, observable, and a skipped run raises an alert
The consent ledger can be replayed to reconstruct the consent state at any past date
A grievance channel is published with a named officer, a contact route and a stated response clock, and the officer is a named role with a current holder rather than an unattributed mailbox
Every data-principal request and every grievance starts a response clock at acknowledgement, and the remaining time is visible to the person who raised it
Missing a response clock raises an escalation to a named owner and is recorded as a breach rather than absorbed
The response clock values come from the versioned, counsel-reviewed jurisdiction profile; when no current profile exists the system fails closed and states that no statutory clock is being asserted
contracts_schema: Consent, rights request and purpose schemas published in the contract and consumed by the clients
Implements the rights-request, status and consent shapes published by T-CON-09; the response clock is a contract field, not an internal one
security_privacy: The consent ledger is append only and its integrity is protected by the audit event service
Rights endpoints require step-up authentication so an account takeover cannot trigger an export or erasure
Requests are rate limited and abuse is recorded
observability: Publishes request counts by type, service level attainment and retention job outcomes without personal data
tests: Negative test proving processing without consent is refused
Consent replay test reconstructing a past state
Erasure propagation test across derived data, caches, vector stores and assistant conversation records
Retention job idempotency test
Step-up bypass attempt test
Response clock start, expiry and escalation test
Missing or expired jurisdiction profile fail-closed test
rollout_rollback: Shipped behind a flag in staging, enabled in production before any beta onboarding
Rollback disables new request intake but never disables the consent gate; the gate is fail-closed
non_goals: Client user interface, which is a separate Android ticket
Crypto-shredding mechanics, which belong to E19
Policy text, which belongs to the compliance pack ticket
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the consent, rights and retention modules and their migrations. Android and web consume the published contract.

items.title: Build pre-onboarding consent, the age gate and the permission dashboard on Android
items.outcome: As a new user, before I hand over anything, I see plainly what is collected and why, I choose each purpose separately, I confirm I am old enough, and I can see and revoke every permission in one place afterwards.
items.context: Onboarding currently reaches data collection before consent exists, and there is no permission dashboard, no age gate and no revocation surface. This is the screen that earns the right to ask for message access later, so it has to be honest and it has to come first.
scope: Pre-onboarding notice in plain language, purpose by purpose, before any collection
Granular per-purpose consent controls with no pre-ticked options
Age confirmation with a documented position on younger users
Versioned age-eligibility policy from T-CMP-04, with launch set to adult-only unless a separately reviewed parental-consent program is approved
Permission dashboard listing each granted permission, what it enables and a revoke control
Revocation and recovery flows, including what the application does after a permission is withdrawn
Consent and purpose surfaces built on the shapes published by T-CON-09, so the pre-onboarding consent screen and the permission dashboard read the same purpose registry the server enforces
acceptance_criteria: No data leaves the device before a consent decision is recorded for the relevant purpose
Each purpose can be refused independently and the application still functions in a reduced, clearly explained way
Declining age confirmation stops onboarding and stores no personal data
The dashboard reflects the real operating system permission state, not a cached copy
Revoking message access from the dashboard or from system settings puts the application in a recoverable state with a clear explanation rather than a crash or a silent failure
All consent screens are fully usable with a screen reader and at the largest text scale
Every purpose shown at pre-onboarding is a purpose identifier and version from the T-CON-09 registry; a locally invented purpose string fails a test
An under-age or unknown-eligibility result stops onboarding before profile creation, retains no entered age detail and provides an accessible explanation and support route
contracts_schema: Consumes the published consent and purpose contract; the copy is rendered from the versioned purpose registry
security_privacy: No analytics events fire before the analytics purpose is consented
The screen states truthfully what stays on the device and this is verified by the traffic inspection harness
observability: Consent decisions recorded as events carrying purpose and version only, never content
tests: Instrumented tests for accept, refuse and partial-consent paths
Permission revocation and recovery tests on the physical device
Accessibility traversal test
Traffic capture confirming no pre-consent egress
Under-age and unknown-eligibility no-profile and no-analytics tests
rollout_rollback: Ships as part of onboarding before any beta invitation is issued
Rollback removes the beta invitation rather than the consent gate
non_goals: Backend consent storage, which is the api ticket
Message permission onboarding specifics, which is an existing Android ticket
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo android. Owns onboarding, the dashboard and the consent screens. The purpose text comes from the published registry and is not written locally.

items.title: Produce the third-party component inventory, payload scrubbing and the data safety declaration
items.outcome: Every third-party component embedded in the application is inventoried and justified, error and analytics payloads are scrubbed at the source, and the published data safety declaration matches captured traffic rather than intent.
items.context: The recommended set of embedded components has never been reconciled with the commitment that no third party can reach message-derived data, and the declaration would otherwise be written from the code's intention. An inaccurate declaration is itself a policy violation and puts the message permission at risk.
scope: Inventory of every embedded component with its purpose, the data it can observe and a justification
Scrubbing hook on the error reporting path with an allowlist rather than a denylist
Push and messaging payload allowlist forbidding monetary values and message content
Declaration mapping each collected data type to a component, a purpose and a retention position
Re-check procedure so the declaration is revalidated on every release
acceptance_criteria: No embedded component can observe message-derived data, demonstrated by the traffic capture evidence
A planted monetary value in an error report is scrubbed before transmission
A push payload containing an amount fails the payload check
Every declared data type maps to an inventoried component and an approved purpose
Adding a new component without an inventory entry fails the pipeline
The declaration and the capture evidence are attached to the release record together
contracts_schema: Inventory and allowlist published as machine-readable files consumed by the traffic inspection harness
security_privacy: Scrubbing is fail-closed; if the hook throws, the report is dropped rather than sent raw
No component receives a user identifier that can be linked to financial records
observability: Publishes component count, scrub drop count and declaration drift per release
tests: Planted value scrubbing test
Push payload allowlist test
New component detection test
Declaration versus capture reconciliation check
rollout_rollback: Blocking for the first public release and for any release adding a component
Rollback is removing the newly added component, not relaxing the check
non_goals: Backend log scrubbing, which the platform ticket owns
Regulatory filings beyond the store declaration
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo android. Owns the inventory, scrubbing hooks and declaration inputs. The docs repository holds only the published policy text.

items.title: Publish the compliance floor pack and rehearse the breach reporting drill
items.outcome: The privacy policy, terms, disclaimers, processor agreements, point of contact and breach runbook are published and accurate before onboarding, and the reporting drill has actually been rehearsed against the clock.
items.context: These obligations are currently scheduled after the beta, and the breach runbook exists as a plan rather than a rehearsed procedure. A six-hour reporting window cannot be met by a team reading a document for the first time during an incident.
scope: Privacy policy and terms accurate to actual system behaviour, versioned and published
Advice-boundary disclaimer text defined once and referenced by every surface that needs it
Processor and sub-processor agreements including any model provider, with disclosure
Point of contact designated and the reporting runbook written with named roles
Tabletop rehearsal of the reporting drill against the required window, with gaps ticketed
Incident severity matrix and user notification templates
Automated reconciliation between the regulatory obligation matrix, the risk-to-ticket matrix and the board, run on a schedule
Versioned, counsel-reviewed jurisdiction profiles as the only source of a statutory value, each with a review date and an expiry
Written India retention opinion reconciling DPDP Rule 6 security records, CERT-In logs, storage limitation, crypto-shredding and restore-safe erasure by data class
Versioned age-eligibility policy stating adult-only launch scope and the separately approved controls required before any parental-consent path may exist
acceptance_criteria: The published policy matches the behaviour recorded by the traffic capture evidence
Every processor that receives personal data has a signed agreement before any data is sent
The drill was executed and the elapsed time to a complete report is recorded against the window
Gaps found in the drill are ticketed with owners rather than noted in prose
The disclaimer text is stored once and consumed by the clients rather than retyped
The on-call owner can state the trigger condition for reporting without consulting the document

The reconciliation check fails when an obligation in compliance/01-regulatory-landscape.md has no owning ticket, when a named risk in product/02-risk-register.md has no owning item, or when a matrix row names a ticket that does not exist
The check fails when a matrix row names a ticket whose status contradicts the matrix, so a closed obligation cannot point at an unstarted ticket

Statutory values - reporting windows, response clocks, retention periods, thresholds - are read from a versioned counsel-reviewed jurisdiction profile, and no such value is written inline in a ticket or a document
An absent or expired jurisdiction profile fails the check and the dependent behaviour fails closed rather than assuming a value
The India profile identifies each retained data class, legal basis, purpose, access role, retention start and end, post-erasure treatment and restore behavior; it cannot express indefinite retention
The check runs on a schedule and its result is visible without opening the board
The region stated in the pack is read from the committed residency policy T-PLT-01 enforces rather than copied into compliance prose
The published age policy fails closed for under-age or unknown eligibility, and family invitations and grants consume the same policy identifier
contracts_schema: Disclaimer and policy version identifiers published so clients can render and record the version shown
Jurisdiction profile published as machine-readable data: jurisdiction, obligation, value, source, counsel reviewer, review date, expiry
Retention profile entries include data class, legal basis, purpose, access policy, period anchor, expiry action, erasure treatment and restore barrier behavior
Age-eligibility policy published as machine-readable data with version, minimum eligibility rule and fail-closed outcome
security_privacy: The pack states exactly what is collected, where it is stored and which region holds it
Nothing in the pack claims a protection that is not implemented and tested
observability: Policy version and acceptance recorded per user without storing the policy text per user
tests: Reconciliation of the policy against captured traffic
Timed tabletop drill with a written outcome
Unowned-obligation failure test
Unowned-risk failure test
Dangling ticket reference failure test
Expired jurisdiction profile fail-closed test
Contradictory or missing DPDP/CERT-In retention and erasure profile failure tests
rollout_rollback: Published before any beta invitation; a policy change requires a version bump and re-acceptance where material
non_goals: Counsel review of expansion markets, which belongs to E20
Implementation of consent storage, which is the api ticket
Reaching a legal conclusion: the profiles record counsel's conclusions and this ticket never derives one
